title: Reality shows: Who is eligible to apply?
questions: Who is eligible to apply?
text:
Ideal cast members are:
* Business owners
* CEOs
* Startup founders
* Entrepreneurs
* Influencers with a business angle
* People actively building businesses, side hustles, brands, or ventures
There is no minimum revenue requirement.
Personality matters. These are reality shows, so we want people who are confident, interesting, competitive, opinionated, charismatic, or otherwise strong on camera.
The opportunity should also be financially appropriate. Someone should be able to comfortably afford the $20,000–$30,000 package plus approximately $3,000–$5,000 in travel/hotel expenses without expecting the show to immediately generate that money back.
conditions: Source designated by project owner; preserve contract-dependent and provisional wording.

title: Reality shows: What does the standard $20,000 package include?
questions: What does the standard $20,000 package include?
text:
The package includes both the reality-show experience and the broader Inside Success media package.
Package overview: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1piWUsDLE4ON9kaHybWoXy3xGWu1PsqoeMBNYn4zz38Y/edit (the documentary benefit placement differs from the newer Call 2 video).
Cast members receive:
* Guaranteed casting in the reality show
* Participation in the main reality series
* Approximately 4–7 episodes per season
* Episodes generally around 25–35 minutes
* Personal cast profile on the official show website
* Professional cast bio
* Individual promotional trailer
* 100,000 guaranteed promotional views on their individual trailer
* Professional behind-the-scenes photos
* 10x Social media reels and clips
* 10x Edited social content
* Movie/show poster assets
* Podcast interview
* Press announcement / PR articles 
* License to use approved footage/content from their participation in their own marketing
* Ability to capture approved personal/social content during filming
* Access to the annual Inside Success awards event
The full personal documentary interview is not a confirmed Standard benefit: see the newer Call 2 video package guidance and its recorded document discrepancy.
conditions: Source designated by project owner; preserve contract-dependent and provisional wording.

title: Reality shows: What does the $30,000 VIP package include?
questions: What does the $30,000 VIP package include?
text:
Package overview: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1piWUsDLE4ON9kaHybWoXy3xGWu1PsqoeMBNYn4zz38Y/edit (the documentary benefit placement differs from the newer Call 2 video).
Everything in the standard package, plus:
* Priority placement on the cast website/page
* 10 additional social media clips (the current Call 2 VIP slide clarifies the written FAQ’s "10x" notation)
* 1x Sit-down 5 min video interview with a producer on set
* Where applicable, access/interview opportunities with celebrity hosts, celebrity guests, or cameos
* Co-executive producer credit, subject to final production/credit terms
* Ability to bring up to two guests instead of one
* One early-elimination immunity advantage for EPISODE 2, meaning the VIP participant cannot be eliminated until Episode 3, described as the halfway mark of the show unless they fail a challenge/don’t participate.
Important: the VIP package does not guarantee that someone wins the competition or remains through the entire season.
The current Call 2 video VIP slide additionally lists a full 20–25 minute documentary interview about the participant/their business. See the recorded discrepancy with the older written package overview before discussing this benefit.
conditions: Source designated by project owner; preserve contract-dependent and provisional wording.

title: Reality shows: Is everyone guaranteed to appear in the show?
questions: Is everyone guaranteed to appear in the show?
text:
Yes.
Every accepted cast member is intended to appear in the series and is guaranteed to make it through the initial episode structure before standard elimination mechanics begin.
Some shows involve:
* elimination
* contestant voting
* challenges
* revenue/performance results
* judging
* team decisions
* other competition mechanics
The exact mechanics vary by show and may intentionally not be disclosed in advance.
conditions: Source designated by project owner; preserve contract-dependent and provisional wording.

title: Reality shows: How much screen time is guaranteed?
questions: How much screen time is guaranteed?
text:
There is no guarantee of an exact number of minutes.
Reality television is edited around what happens during production. Some cast members will naturally appear more than others depending on:
* performance
* story
* challenges
* relationships
* conflict
* entertainment value
* elimination timing
The intention is to feature the cast broadly throughout the series, but final editorial decisions remain with production.
conditions: Source designated by project owner; preserve contract-dependent and provisional wording.

title: Reality shows: What happens if someone is eliminated?
questions: What happens if someone is eliminated?
text:
They still receive the rest of their contracted media package.
That includes applicable:
* podcast
* documentary interview
* promotional trailer
* cast page
* photos
* social content
* PR
* branding assets
They may also remain around production for the remainder of filming where appropriate.
If they want the full production experience after elimination, they may be able to:
* observe filming
* assist with production
* help with props or scenes
* see behind-the-scenes production
* work remotely during downtime
conditions: Source designated by project owner; preserve contract-dependent and provisional wording.

title: Reality shows: How long is filming & shot location?
questions: How long is filming & shot location?
text:
Most shows will film for approximately:
7–14 consecutive days
Some larger concepts may require closer to two weeks.
Participants should block the entire filming period because schedules remain dynamic.
There will often be downtime between scenes, setups, interviews, challenges, etc., but cast members need to remain available.
Daily call sheets/agendas may be provided approximately the day before depending on production requirements.
LOCATION - Either Florida or Caribbean for most part. Small chance of LA or elsewhere for tax/rebate purposes. Confirmed once cast are finalized. Some shows may feature a celebrity guest/judge/host - so location has to stay flexible until casting is finished.
conditions: Source designated by project owner; preserve contract-dependent and provisional wording.

title: Reality shows: Could they need to return after filming?
questions: Could they need to return after filming?
text:
Possibly.
There may be a need for approximately 1–2 additional filming days later for:
* inserts
* pickup shots
* interviews
* missing scenes
* continuity
* post-production requirements
This is not always necessary, but cast members should understand that it is possible.
conditions: Source designated by project owner; preserve contract-dependent and provisional wording.

title: Reality shows: When will filming take place?
questions: When will filming take place?
text:
Current productions are expected to begin late 2026 and continue through 2027.
Exact dates depend on:

* location availability
* production scheduling
* show format
Participants will generally receive at least 60 days' notice of their confirmed filming dates.

title: Reality shows: Where will filming take place?

title: Reality shows: Who pays for travel?
questions: Who pays for travel?
text:
The cast member is responsible for:

* Hotel

Inside Success covers:
* Production costs
* Filming
* Crew
* Editing
* PR included in the package

title: Reality shows: Can they continue working while filming?
questions: Can they continue working while filming?
text:
Participants must treat filming as the priority during the production window.
There may be significant downtime where they can:
* use their laptop
* answer emails

* work remotely
However, production may call them at any time during scheduled filming days.
For certain concepts, phones, laptops, internet access, or outside communication may also be intentionally restricted as part of the show's rules.

questions: What happens if they cannot attend the filming dates?

If they cannot attend after the date is announced, they can generally transfer their participation to:
* Another upcoming Inside Success reality show
* A future season of the same show, if produced
* Another qualifying Inside Success media program
Season 2 transfers would receive priority where applicable.

questions: What happens if the show itself is delayed or canceled?

Possible alternatives include:
* Another reality-show format
* A future season
* Legacy Makers
* Women in Power
* Podcast/media package

The commercial intention is that the participant retains the value of their purchase even if the original production cannot proceed.

title: Reality shows: What distribution is guaranteed?
questions: What distribution is guaranteed?
text:
This needs extremely precise sales language.
Based on what you described, the safe internal structure is:
Guaranteed:
* Inside Success TV distribution
* Whatever external platform your contract specifically guarantees
Not appropriate to promise casually:
* Netflix
* Hulu
* Amazon Prime Video
* Apple TV
* any particular third-party platform
unless that exact platform is contractually secured for that particular show.
I would not let reps say:
"You'll definitely be on Netflix, Amazon, Hulu or Apple."
That is legally dangerous if the actual platform has not yet been selected/contracted.
Better:
"The series is guaranteed distribution through Inside Success TV plus at least one qualifying external streaming/distribution platform as defined in your agreement. We also pitch selected original formats to major streamers and distribution partners."
Then separately, where truthful:
"Previous Inside Success programming has appeared on platforms such as Amazon Prime Video and Apple TV."
The distinction between distribution and being pitched to Netflix needs to be hammered into training.
conditions: Source designated by project owner; preserve contract-dependent and provisional wording.

title: Reality shows: What views are guaranteed?

100,000 promotional views on each cast member's individual trailer.

* guaranteed episode viewers

* guaranteed streamer viewers
* guaranteed buyers/leads
* guaranteed business revenue
The broader show may receive millions of paid promotional impressions/views collectively, but only the contractual guarantee should be represented as guaranteed.

title: Reality shows: Is this intended to immediately make the participant money?

No.
This should actually be stated explicitly during sales.
The primary value is:
* brand building
* authority
* media assets
* content
* TV experience
* PR
* visibility
* networking
* personal positioning
It is not an investment product and should not be presented as something expected to produce an immediate financial return.

title: Reality shows: Is the show REAL? Will it be hard? Can I get hurt? Will I lose money?
questions: Is the show REAL? Will it be hard? Can I get hurt? Will I lose money?
text:
These are real reality shows, no fake, so yes, there maybe harder elements depending on the show, participants have to be willing to commit to the process to make great tv. 
For example:

- KID CEO - The Kid is in charge of the business, and may make bad decisions that cost the company money, upset staff members etc, these cant be faked (but parameters are in place if they wanted to do something illegal or catastrophic, etc).
- ISLAND SHOW - Participants must survive and “rough it” - so yes, they may become hungry, sunburnt, dehydrated, have to walk long distances, physical exercises, etc - medical supervisors will be on site for support, and all participants have to sign waivers.
These shows aren’t designed to make the cast members suffer 24/7, its more to display HUSTLE, ENTREPRENEURSHIP, LEADERSHIP, PROBLEM SOLVING, BUSINESS, etc, but at same time, we do want some drama and wow moments to make good TV. Ultimately, the better the show becomes, the more the CAST WINS as they will get more views, etc.
conditions: Source designated by project owner; preserve contract-dependent and provisional wording.

title: Reality documentary interview: VIP in current Call 2 presentation; written FAQ discrepancy
questions: Is the Legacy Makers documentary in Standard or VIP?
What does the reality VIP upgrade include?
Why do the reality package PDF and video differ?

title: Current commission invoicing SOP: HubSpot ledger and Bill.com
text: Commissions are tracked in the Payment Commission Tracker and HubSpot. After the first sale, request a Bill.com invitation through #sales-finance-requests and complete the vendor profile and ACH banking details. In HubSpot use Reporting > Reports > Ledger, filter the commission period and owner, then Apply. Submit invoices through Bill.com twice monthly: the 16th for the 1st–15th, and the 1st of the following month for the remaining period. Include both new-sales cash collected and recurring/installment commissions, with line items such as client name and commission amount, and attach the HubSpot ledger screenshot for the period. Use Net 30 terms, meaning due 30 days after invoice submission, and track payment status in Bill.com. ACH only; no physical checks. Questions about missing or incorrect commission go to #sales-finance-requests or #sales-tech-requests; Michael Kumov is the finance contact. This replaces the old Keap screenshot instructions for this invoicing process, not every unrelated Keap procedure.
conditions: Apply only to the stated process and scope.

title: Reapplying: preserve context and conflicting intervals
text: Main ISTV ordinary reapplication: the prior source adjudication identifies Rich’s minimum of three months for a no-show, missed ordinary Call 2 decision deadline, rejection or not-fit outcome. This does not automatically permit reapplication or override documented exceptions or repeated-abuse handling. Preserve the separately reviewed six-month VIP/Lite case where payment was not completed before the cohort closed (July 27). A September 8 Sales Ops reply says 3–6 months in a mixed missed-main-cohort/reality recommendation thread, but does not establish an explicit replacement for Rich’s normal rule. Reality competition reapplication is a separate six-month statement in its Call 2 video. Determine the show and missed-decision versus closed-cohort-payment context; do not flatten them into one universal wait. The retained non-duration instruction from the older missed-Call-1 guidance is not to read the application’s banned/blacklisted language verbatim; a missed call alone does not establish permanent blacklisting. Repeated-abuse handling remains a separate decision.
conditions: Rich controls the normal main ISTV three-month minimum, including the ordinary missed Call 2 payment/signature deadline. The superseded records contain already-adjudicated conflicting intervals and are not current exceptions. The separately reviewed July 27 VIP/Lite closed-cohort-payment rule and reality six-month rule remain distinct; do not apply either to every missed ordinary deadline.

title: Coaching: spouse or business partner needs to join
text: The training identifies decision-maker involvement before Call 2 as a way to avoid preventable follow-up delays. Useful coaching: ask early who else needs to be involved; when a spouse or partner concern appears later, ask what questions remain and offer to include them in a conversation. Example: “Of course. What would they need to understand to make this decision with you? We can cover those questions together.” Help distinguish fit, budget, timing and missing information without accusing the prospect of lying or undermining their relationship. Do not invent a deposit requirement, deadline or price from an old training example.
conditions: Coaching synthesis must not create or change company terms.

title: Coaching: prospect wants attorney review
text: The training distinguishes an unanswered contract question from a request for legal review. Ask which terms the prospect wants clarified, explain the actual supported terms, and arrange the applicable follow-up process. Respect their choice to seek independent advice. Do not claim the agreement is risk-free, that no legal disputes exist, that every redline is forbidden, or that payment must precede review based only on this older training video. Apply current show-specific contract-review rules; the reality contract workflow may differ from the main-show workflow.
conditions: Coaching synthesis must not create or change company terms.

title: Coaching: concerns about bad reviews or legitimacy
text: Ask which specific review or claim concerns the prospect and help separate the exact company, service and experience being discussed. Offer relevant verified evidence and explain what the customer is paying for in their actual package. Acknowledge the concern without dismissing all critics as rejected applicants or asserting unverified customer counts, lawsuit history, testimonials or celebrity endorsements. Example: “I understand why that would give you pause. Which part concerns you most? Let’s look at the specific claim and the written details of what this includes.”
conditions: Coaching synthesis must not create or change company terms.

title: Coaching: value and ROI questions
text: Ask what the prospect wants to accomplish and discuss supported deliverables and how they could use those assets. Do not promise or imply revenue, customer acquisition, profitability or guaranteed return. A disclaimer does not make a numerical or hypothetical ROI pitch acceptable. Example: “I can walk through the content and usage rights included, so you can judge whether those assets fit your plans. I can’t promise that participation will generate customers or revenue.” The old objection-handling video mentions weekly marketing support and historical package prices; those statements are not current offer authority.
conditions: Coaching synthesis must not create or change company terms.

title: HubSpot: fields to update after meetings
text: The current meeting-status walkthrough shows updating the meeting outcome (such as no-show, sold, or green light approved) and the number of the call that actually happened (first, second, third or completed call). For a sale enter total cash collected and total contracted. For a green light enter the green light score, relevant notes and the urgent-request flag when applicable. Mark double booking when applicable. Use Today’s Meetings, Yesterday’s Meetings or the week’s meeting tab to find the record. Keep Google Calendar connected. Numerical amounts in the demonstration are examples, not approved package prices. Recording an urgent flag does not itself guarantee a turnaround time.

title: Current company context: show families and CRM
text: Inside Success TV’s regular documentary offers (including Legacy Makers, Women in Power and America’s Best Doctors) are main ISTV. Daymond John and Next Level CEO (NLCEO) belong to the separate DJ/NLCEO family, not main ISTV. The new reality competition family includes Business Race, Entrepreneurs Island, Startup Lockdown, Flipping for Fortune, Millionaire Match House, Love or Business, Mansion of Money, and Kids CEO; Kids CEO was subsequently paused on September 10. Reality terms do not inherit the regular documentary prices, package entitlements, cohort or onboarding rules. HubSpot is now the company CRM for current lead, call and meeting work. Keap references in older training are historical; they do not establish the current HubSpot screen path. Use current scoped policies for each specific procedure.
conditions: Catalog context, not a grant of cross-show entitlement or a claim of real-time application availability.
